blocks.text: The UGE WCH-LinkE Debugger PCB is a precision-designed printed circuit board intended for building a high-performance WCH-LinkE programmer/debugger compatible with WCH’s RISC-V and ARM microcontrollers, such as the CH32V series and CH32F series.
It allows developers and students to flash firmware, debug applications, and communicate via UART, all from a compact and reliable USB-powered interface.

Getting Started Guide for WCH-LinkE Debugger (DIY Version)
Based on CH32V305FBP6 – Designed by UGE Electronics
The WCH-LinkE Debugger is a versatile programmer and debugger interface designed for WCH RISC-V and ARM microcontrollers, including the CH32V, CH32F, and CH57x families.
It provides SWD/JTAG and UART communication for programming, debugging, and serial logging.

This DIY version uses the CH32V305FBP6 MCU, SC662 3.3V regulator, and a 12 MHz crystal oscillator for reliable operation. Once assembled and flashed with official WCH-LinkE firmware, it works exactly like the factory WCH-LinkE.

A quartz crystal provides both series and parallel resonance. The series resonance is a few kilohertz lower than the parallel one. Crystals below 30 MHz are generally operated between series and parallel resonance, which means that the crystal appears as an inductive reactance in operation, this inductance forming a parallel resonant circuit with externally connected parallel capacitance. Any small additional capacitance in parallel with the crystal will thus pull the frequency downwards. Moreover, the effective inductive reactance of the crystal can be reduced by adding a capacitor in series with the crystal. This latter technique can provide a useful method of trimming the oscillatory frequency within a narrow range; in this case inserting a capacitor in series with the crystal will raise the frequency of oscillation. For a crystal to operate at its specified frequency, the electronic circuit has to be exactly that specified by the crystal manufacturer. Note that these points imply a subtlety concerning crystal oscillators in this frequency range: the crystal does not usually oscillate at precisely either of its resonant frequencies.

Crystals above 30 MHz (up to >200 MHz) are generally operated at series resonance where the impedance appears at its minimum and equal to the series resistance. For these crystals the series resistance is specified (<100 Ω) instead of the parallel capacitance. To reach higher frequencies, a crystal can be made to vibrate at one of its overtone modes, which occur near multiples of the fundamental resonant frequency. Only odd numbered overtones are used. Such a crystal is referred to as a 3rd, 5th, or even 7th overtone crystal. To accomplish this, the oscillator circuit usually includes additional LC circuits to select the desired overtone.

A ceramic resonator is an electronic component consisting of a piece of a piezoelectric ceramic material with two or more metal electrodes attached. When connected in an electronic oscillator circuit, resonant mechanical vibrations in the device generate an oscillating signal of a specific frequency. Like the similar quartz crystal, they are used in crystal oscillators for purposes such as generating the clock signal used to control timing in computers and other digital logic devices.

Ceramic resonators are made of high-stability piezoelectric ceramics, generally lead zirconium titanate (PZT) which functions as a mechanical resonator. In operation, mechanical vibrations induce an oscillating voltage in the attached electrodes due to the piezoelectricity of the material. The thickness of the ceramic substrate determines the resonant frequency of the device.

blocks.text: The USB-to-RS-232 converter cable provides a bridge between modern USB ports and legacy RS-232 serial devices. It enables a computer without a built-in serial (DB9) port to communicate with older peripherals such as modems, barcode scanners, industrial controllers, and more. The conversion is done via integrated electronics in the cable, making it appear to the host computer as a standard serial port once installed.

This cable is designed for ease of use: simply plug the USB-A end into a PC and the DB9 male connector into your RS-232 device. Once connected, the built-in chipset (such as PL2303 or FTDI) handles serial-to-USB data translation, managing the voltage level shifting and protocol conversion. Because the cable is bus-powered, there’s no need for an external power supply, making installation clean and portable.

In operation, the adapter maintains reliable serial communication at a wide range of baud rates, enabling legacy hardware to work seamlessly with newer computers. Whether you’re working in a lab, industrial environment, or running point-of-sale equipment, the converter cable offers a cost-effective and practical solution for integrating RS-232 systems into modern computing environments. Its durable design ensures stable connectivity even under extended use.
Converts USB port to RS-232 DB9 serial interface.
Utilizes common USB-to-serial chipsets (e.g., PL2303, FTDI) for broad compatibility.
Supports a wide variety of serial settings (baud rate, parity, stop bits).
Bus-powered no external power adapter required.

Heart Rate click carries Maxim’s MAX30100 integrated pulse oximetry and a heart-rate sensor. It’s an optical sensor that derives its readings from emitting two wavelengths of light from two LEDs – a red and an infrared one – then measuring the absorbance of pulsing blood through a photodetector. This particular LED color combination is optimized for reading the data through the tip of one’s finger.

The signal is processed by a low-noise analog signal processing unit and communicated to the target MCU through the mikroBUS I2C interface. blocks.text: The TLP250 arrives as a compact, 8-lead DIP optocoupler built around a GaAlAs LED and an integrated photodetector. Its design communicates purposefulness: a small, self-contained module that isolates control and power domains while packaging the drive circuitry in a familiar DIP footprint. The body feels utilitarian and immediately signals that it belongs on a designer’s workbench or inside a power electronics module.

Physically modest yet mechanically robust, the device presents the tidy geometry of through-hole components and a clear pin assignment that makes it straightforward to wire into gate-drive circuits. A recommended bypass capacitor between VCC and GND is emphasized in the layout guidance, underlining that the part is intended to be used as an active, stabilized driver rather than a passive coupler.

When seen in context – mounted on a PCB driving an IGBT or power MOSFET – the TLP250 reads as an engineered interface: an electromechanical handshake that translates low-power LED signals into substantial push/pull output currents while preserving galvanic isolation. Its presence simplifies the board-level layout for gate-drive stages and gives designers a clearly defined building block for switching power systems.

The Arduino Nano 33 IoT is a compact Arduino BLE WiFi board built for connected projects — one of the few Nano-sized boards that combines both wireless protocols on a single module. Instead of choosing between a WiFi-only or Bluetooth-only board, this one gives you both, plus a 6-axis motion sensor and a dedicated security chip, all in a form factor small enough to fit into space-limited builds.

At its core is a low-power SAMD21 processor — a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M0+ chip known for a good balance of performance and battery efficiency. Wireless connectivity comes from a u-blox NINA module handling both WiFi and Bluetooth Low Energy, while a separate ATECC608A security chip handles encrypted communication, useful for any project connecting to a cloud service or handling sensitive data. An onboard 6-axis IMU (accelerometer + gyroscope) rounds out the board, making it a practical choice for motion-based projects like pedometers, vibration alerts, or basic robotics orientation sensing — without needing a separate sensor module.

Setting up a WiFi connection on this board follows the standard Arduino WiFi library pattern — connect to an existing network, or configure the board to broadcast its own access point. Beyond local networking, the board can also connect to cloud platforms for remote monitoring and control, including Arduino's own cloud service as well as third-party platforms commonly used in IoT projects. This makes it a practical arduino wifi board choice for projects that need to send sensor data somewhere beyond the local network — home automation dashboards, remote monitoring systems, or simple data-logging projects that report back to a phone or web app.

What sets this board apart from most microcontroller boards is that its wireless chipset can act as both a Bluetooth host and a Bluetooth client — meaning it can either connect out to other Bluetooth devices or accept incoming connections, using the same hardware. That flexibility matters for projects like a Bluetooth-connected wearable that talks to a phone app, or a central hub that pulls data in from several Bluetooth Low Energy sensors at once.
Need longer range instead of short-range WiFi/Bluetooth? The Arduino MKR WAN 1310 uses the same SAMD21 processor but adds LoRaWAN connectivity for long-distance IoT projects.

What makes this different from other Arduino Nano boards?

It's one of the few Nano-format boards with both WiFi and Bluetooth Low Energy built in on the same module, along with a dedicated security chip and motion sensor — features usually spread across multiple separate boards or add-on modules.
Do I need external hardware to use WiFi and Bluetooth together?
No — both are handled by the onboard u-blox NINA module, so no additional wireless shield or module is required.
What is the ATECC608A chip used for?
It's a secure element dedicated to handling encrypted communication, useful for projects connecting to cloud services where secure authentication matters.
Can this board be used for motion-sensing projects without an extra sensor?
Yes — the built-in 6-axis IMU (LSM6DS3) can handle basic motion sensing tasks like vibration detection or orientation tracking without any additional hardware.
Does the board come with a USB cable?
No, the board ships without a USB cable, so you'll need to supply your own to program it or provide power over USB.

blocks.text: Photoresist Stripper Solution 100mL for Electronic Photoresist PCBs

✅ A ready-to-use Photoresist Stripper Solution (100 mL) designed for the final stripping stage of positive photoresist PCB fabrication. Use it after copper etching to remove the remaining resist layer and reveal clean, bright copper artwork. Works at room temperature, needs no dilution, and is non-corrosive to copper. A single bottle is typically enough to strip photoresist areas totaling up to ~600 cm² in just about 5 minutes with light brushing and proper rinsing.
🛡️ Copper-safe formula — strips photoresist without thinning copper traces.
⏱️ Fast at room temperature — removes the coating layer in only a few minutes, no heaters required.
🧪 No mixing — consistent, pre-set strength; pour a small amount into a plastic or glass tray and go.
🧰 Lab & home friendly — low hassle workflow for classrooms, makerspaces, repair benches, and prototyping labs.
📏 Efficient coverage — 100 mL comfortably handles up to ~600 cm² of board area, ideal for small runs and frequent prototyping.
🧴 Practical bottle — tight cap, compact footprint, clear solution for easy visual inspection.
🔧 Use only after etching: Once unprotected copper is etched, rinse the board thoroughly, then strip the remaining resist to leave bare copper ready for soldering, plating, or protective coating.
🔁 Part of a 3-chemistry workflow: Exposure → Developing → Etching → Stripping. This solution is step five in the visual guides.
✅ Bright, even copper finish — pads and tracks become uniformly visible.
✅ Predictable timing — ~5 minutes typical at room temperature with gentle agitation.
✅ Simple, repeatable steps — rinse → pour → immerse → light brush → final rinse.
✅ Compatible with positive dry film & presensitized boards — same reliable result across common brands.
✅ Low learning curve — forgiving window for hobbyists and students.
✅ Supports rework — safely removes resist from boards that need post-etch edits.
⚙️ 1) Rinse after etch: Wash the PCB thoroughly with water to stop etchant action and remove residues (very important).
⚙️ 2) Pour a small amount: Shake bottle gently, then dispense into a plastic/glass tray. Do not dilute with water.
⚙️ 3) Immerse at room temp: Place the board flat; keep solution moving with a soft brush or gentle rocking.
⚙️ 4) Wait ~5 minutes: Continue smooth brushing until the pink/green/blue resist layer lifts off fully.
⚙️ 5) Final rinse: Rinse well with water to stop the reaction and reveal clean copper. Dry with lint-free wipes or air.
💡 Never heat directly: If faster action is needed, indirectly warm the sealed bottle in 30–40 °C water for a short time; do not apply direct heat.
💡 Use light-colored trays: Easier to see flakes of resist lifting off.
💡 Brush quality matters: A soft, non-metallic brush or foam swab accelerates stripping evenly without scratching copper.
💡 Protect vias and edges: Keep the board flat to avoid pooling that can trap residues near cut edges.
💡 Post-strip prep: After rinsing, consider micro-abrasion or alcohol wipe to ensure perfect solderability.
🧤 Wear disposable gloves; avoid skin and eye contact.
🌬️ Work in a ventilated area and avoid breathing any vapors or aerosols.
🧒 Keep tightly closed and out of reach of children.
🚯 Dispose of spent solution according to local regulations for photo-chemicals.
🚫 Do not mix with other chemicals; do not store near heat or direct sunlight.

محلول كَشْط الريزست الضوئي 100 مل لصناعة لوحات الدوائر المطبوعة

✅ محلول إزالة الريزست (100 مل) جاهز للاستخدام لمرحلة الكشط النهائية في تصنيع لوحات الدوائر المطبوعة بالريزست الإيجابي. يُستخدم بعد عملية الحفر لإزالة طبقة الريزست المتبقية وكشف النحاس لامعًا بوضوح. يعمل عند درجة حرارة الغرفة، لا يحتاج إلى التخفيف، وهو غير مُتآكل للنحاس. زجاجة واحدة تكفي عادةً لكشط طبقات تغطية بمساحة إجمالية حتى ~600 سم² خلال حوالي 5 دقائق مع تحريك لطيف وفرشاة ناعمة وشطف جيّد.
🛡️ لطيف على النحاس — يزيل الريزست دون ترقيق المسارات.
⏱️ سريع بدون تسخين — بضع دقائق عند حرارة الغرفة.
🧪 جاهز بلا خلط — صُب كمية قليلة في صينية بلاستيكية أو زجاجية وابدأ فورًا.
🧰 مناسب للمعامل والمنزل — خطوات بسيطة لبيئات التعليم والهواة والمختبرات.
📏 تغطية فعّالة — 100 مل تكفي حتى ~600 سم²، مثالية للنماذج الأولية والدفعات الصغيرة.
🧴 زجاجة عملية — غطاء محكم، سائل شفاف لتتبّع تقدّم الإزالة.
🔧 يُستخدم بعد الحفر مباشرةً: بعد إزالة النحاس غير المحمي، اشطف اللوحة جيدًا، ثم قم بالكشط لإزالة ما تبقّى من الريزست وتهيئة النحاس للحام أو الطلاء أو الحماية.
🔁 جزء من سلسلة كيميائية: التعريض → الإظهار → الحفر → الكشط. هذا المحلول هو المرحلة الخامسة في المخططات المصوّرة.
✅ سطح نحاس لامع ومتجانس — تظهر البادات والمسارات بوضوح تام.
✅ توقيت متوقع — ≈5 دقائق عند حرارة الغرفة مع تحريك خفيف.
✅ خطوات قليلة قابلة للتكرار — شطف → صب → غمر → فرشاة ناعمة → شطف نهائي.
✅ توافق واسع — مع الفيلم الضوئي الإيجابي والألواح المُحضّرة مسبقًا.
✅ منحنى تعلم منخفض — مناسب للطلاب والمبتدئين.
✅ يدعم أعمال الإصلاح — يزيل الريزست بأمان عند الحاجة لتعديلات ما بعد الحفر.

blocks.text: P87C055BBPNB TV & Video Controller 600mil IC DIP-42

The P87C055BBPNB is a dedicated microcontroller designed by Philips Semiconductors specifically for television and video (MTV) applications. It is derived from the industry-standard 80C51 microcontroller core but is optimized to serve as the central control unit in TV receivers and tuners, integrating specialized functions not found in generic microcontrollers.

A key feature of this controller is its advanced integrated On-Screen Display (OSD) subsystem. It includes a dedicated character generator ROM, dual-ported display RAM, and logic to superimpose text and graphics onto a video signal. The OSD offers flexible formatting, multiple shadowing modes, and per-character color selection, allowing for the creation of sophisticated menus and information displays directly on the TV screen.

The device provides extensive analog control capabilities via multiple Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) digital-to-analog converters, including eight 6-bit PWMs and one high-precision 14-bit PWM (TDAC). The P87C055 variant features One-Time Programmable (OTP) EPROM memory, allowing for user programming of both the application code and the OSD character font set, enabling customization and prototyping.

blocks.text: The RHRP15120 is a hyper fast power diode built for demanding switching environments. Housed in a TO-220AC flange, it uses silicon-nitride passivation and ion-implanted epitaxial planar construction to deliver consistent, rugged performance. Its soft-recovery behavior keeps turn-off ringing and electrical noise low, helping protect and reduce stress on switching transistors.

Designed to minimize stored charge, the device recovers faster than many ultrafast diodes, improving efficiency in high-frequency converters. Robust thermal characteristics and avalanche-rated construction give resilience against transient energy events, while low junction capacitance reduces switching distortion. These attributes help produce stable, predictable behavior across duty cycles.

Balancing high voltage endurance with substantial forward-current capability, the RHRP15120 is suited for freewheeling, clamping and rectification duties in compact power assemblies. The TO-220 mounting and favorable thermal resistance simplify heatsinking and thermal management, making board layout and integration straightforward for power designers.

يُعرف هذا النوع أيضًا باسم موتور الاهتزاز القرصي، ويُستخدم في التطبيقات التي تحتاج إلى تنبيه اهتزازي أو إشعار صامت أو استجابة لمسية دون الحاجة إلى أجزاء ميكانيكية كبيرة أو آليات خارجية معقدة. ولهذا السبب فهو مناسب جدًا للمنتجات الصغيرة التي تعتمد على إشارات اهتزاز بسيطة وواضحة.

تم تصميم آر سي دي 1027 خصيصًا للأجهزة الخفيفة التي يتم ارتداؤها أو حملها باليد، حيث يوفر اهتزازًا مناسبًا للتنبيه أو التفاعل اللمسي عند العمل بالقرب من المستخدم. ويعمل ضمن مدى من 1.5 إلى 3.7 فولت تيار مستمر، مع جهد اسمي 3 فولت، ويقدم سرعة تقريبية 11000 ± 2500 لفة في الدقيقة، مما يجعله مناسبًا لتطبيقات الاهتزاز في الأجهزة الصغيرة.

يتميز هذا الموتور بأبعاد صغيرة جدًا، حيث يبلغ قطره 10 مم فقط، بينما يبلغ سمكه 2.7 مم، لذلك فهو مناسب للمشروعات التي تتطلب مكونًا نحيفًا وخفيفًا. كما يأتي مزودًا بأسلاك توصيل، حيث يكون السلك الأحمر للموجب والسلك الأسود للسالب، مما يسهل عملية التوصيل داخل الدوائر الإلكترونية.
إذا كنت تحتاج إلى موتور اهتزاز صغير وعملي لإضافة وظيفة تنبيه أو تفاعل لمسي داخل جهاز محمول أو مشروع إلكتروني صغير، فإن هذا الموديل يُعد اختيارًا مناسبًا من حيث الحجم وسهولة الاستخدام.

Designed around the power requirements of Raspberry Pi 5, it provides the special 5.1V / 5A power profile needed to support demanding workloads and higher-power USB peripherals, while also supporting standard USB Power Delivery profiles for compatible USB-C devices.

This is an original Raspberry Pi power supply rather than a generic USB-C charger. It is designed to correctly negotiate the high-current USB-C PD power mode supported by Raspberry Pi 5.

Its construction also makes it useful in applications that require light mechanical separation, surface protection, anti-abrasion layering, and added dielectric support inside electrical products. ورق عزل شعيري لاصق من الجهتين بعرض 100 مم وطول 1 متر وسمك 0.2 مم

ورق العزل الشعيري اللاصق من الجهتين بعرض 100 مم وطول 1 متر وسمك 0.2 مم هو خامة عملية مخصصة لأعمال العزل الكهربائي، وتجميع حزم البطاريات، وحماية المكونات الداخلية في التطبيقات الإلكترونية والصناعية المختلفة. يعتمد هذا المنتج على ورق عزل شعيري مع طبقة لاصقة من الجهتين، مما يساعد على تثبيته بسهولة بين الخلايا، والأسطح المعدنية، وطبقات العزل، والأجزاء الداخلية التي تحتاج إلى فصل كهربائي مع تثبيت جيد في نفس الوقت.

يأتي المنتج بعرض 100 مم وسمك 0.2 مم، وهي مواصفات مناسبة لتوفير توازن جيد بين المرونة، وقوة الاستخدام، وكفاءة العزل. كما يمكن قصه بسهولة حسب المقاس المطلوب، لذلك فهو مناسب جدًا لأعمال الإنتاج، والصيانة، والإصلاح، وتجهيز النماذج الأولية. وبما أنه يُباع بالمتر الواحد، فهو يوفّر مرونة أكبر للعميل الذي يحتاج كمية مناسبة للعمل الفعلي دون الحاجة إلى شراء رول كامل.

يُستخدم هذا النوع من ورق العزل بشكل واسع في تجميع بطاريات الليثيوم، خاصة في الأماكن التي تحتاج إلى طبقة عزل ثابتة بين الخلايا أو بين البطارية والأجزاء المعدنية أو بين الطبقات الداخلية المختلفة. كما أن وجود لاصق على الجهتين يساعد على تثبيت الورق في مكانه أثناء التجميع ويقلل من الحركة أو الانزلاق بعد التركيب.

وإلى جانب استخدامه في البطاريات، يمكن الاستفادة منه أيضًا في تطبيقات العزل الداخلي داخل الأجهزة، أو كطبقة حماية بين الأسطح، أو كفاصل عازل داخل وحدات التجميع المختلفة. لذلك فهو مناسب للفنيين، ومصنّعي البطاريات، والعاملين في الصيانة، وكل من يحتاج خامة عزل عملية وسهلة الاستخدام داخل الورشة أو خط الإنتاج.

blocks.text: TM1637 4 Bits Digital Tube LED Display Module With Clock Display for Arduino HW-069

This 7 segment LED Display has 4 digits which are controlled by TM1637 Driver Chip. It requires only two connections to control this TM1637 4 Bits Digital Tube LED Display Module. The module is a 12-foot clock with four common anode tube (0.36 inch) display module for driver IC TM1637, only two signal lines can make the MCU control four 7-segment digital tubes.
There are several modules using this TM1637 chip to form a 4 digit numerical display module. TM1637 has also keyboard input capability but is not used in this module.

blocks.text: Arduino Leonardo — ATmega32U4 Board with Native USB HID, 20 I/O, 7 PWM

Meet Arduino Leonardo—the classic 5 V development board built around the ATmega32U4 with native USB. Unlike boards that rely on a separate USB-to-serial chip, Leonardo talks USB directly, so it can appear to your computer as a keyboard, mouse, gamepad, MIDI device, or a virtual COM port—all from your sketch. This makes it a favorite for human-interface projects, creative controllers, automation, data-logging, and STEM classrooms where rapid iteration matters.
✅ Native USB HID: emulate keyboard/mouse/MIDI without extra firmware or bridges.
🔌 Plug & upload: micro-USB programming with auto reset; works with the modern Arduino IDE.
🧠 ATmega32U4 @ 16 MHz: 32 KB flash (≈28 KB usable), 2.5 KB SRAM, 1 KB EEPROM.
🧲 Versatile I/O: 20 digital I/O, 7 PWM, up to 12 analog inputs; UART, I²C, SPI, external interrupts.

The charging process is divided into the following three processes: trickle mode, constant current mode and constant voltage mode. When the battery voltage is lower than 3V, the charging module is in trickle mode, and the charging current is 300mA; When the battery voltage is greater than 3V, the charging module enters the constant current mode. At this time, it is charged at full speed according to the set target current, and the power can be about 21W; When the battery voltage rises to the charging target voltage (for example, 4.2V), the charging module enters the constant voltage mode. At this time, the current gradually decreases while the battery terminal voltage remains unchanged; When the charging current decreases to the charging cut-off current, the charging ends. After charging, if the battery voltage decreases to 0.1V lower than the target voltage, the charging is automatically restarted. (Note: if the voltage exceeds 4.2V, it is normal and the battery will not be damaged. If the voltage is 4.2V, the lamp is still flashing, it means that the battery is not fully charged. Full charge is not only based on the charging voltage.)

The VL53L0X is a next-generation Time-of-Flight (ToF) laser-ranging module,
housed in the smallest package on the market. Unlike conventional infrared sensors that measure
reflected light intensity, the VL53L0X measures the actual travel time of light
to calculate distance. This ensures precise distance mapping regardless of the target’s color,
reflectivity, or surface texture, making it far superior to standard IR and ultrasonic sensors.
940nm Laser Technology: Uses an invisible, Class 1 eye-safe vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL).
Precise ToF Measurement: Measures absolute range up to 2 meters, unaffected by target reflectance.
High-Quality Purple PCB: Compact design with integrated voltage regulation and logic level shifters for 3.3V/5V compatibility.
Fast & Accurate: Supports multiple ranging modes, including high-speed (20ms) and high-accuracy (200ms) modes.

SCL / SDA: I2C Clock and Data lines.
XSHUT: Shutdown pin (Active Low). Pull high to enable the sensor.
Robotics: Obstacle avoidance and wall-following for drones and RC cars.
User Interfaces: 1D touchless gesture control and proximity detection.
Consumer Electronics: Camera autofocus enhancement and proximity sensing in smartphones.
Industrial: Tank level sensing and automated counting systems.

ekostra-29880.summary: DC Motor GA25-370 12V with Encoder 80 RPM 1. Voltage: 12V DC 2. Speed: 80 RPM (no-load) 3. Gearbox: GA25 (metal) 4. Encoder: Incremental quadrature 5. Motor: 370 size

blocks.text: The DC Motor GA25-370 12V with Encoder is a high-torque DC gearmotor featuring a GA25 gearbox and a 370-sized motor. It is designed to provide a no-load speed of 80 RPM at 12V, making it an excellent choice for applications that demand substantial low-end torque and precise control. The integrated quadrature encoder allows for real-time feedback on position and speed.

The encoder outputs two distinct channels (A and B) that are used to determine the direction of rotation and the motor’s velocity. This feedback is vital for implementing closed-loop control systems, enabling the motor to maintain a constant speed or reach a specific position accurately. The metal gear train in the GA25 gearbox ensures minimal backlash and high durability, suitable for heavy-duty robotic tasks and automated machinery.

ekostra-29088.summary: AMS1117 3.3V Power Module Board HW-122 1. Main Chip: AMS1117-3.3 2. Output Voltage: 3.3V (Fixed) 3. Max Output Current: 800mA 4. Input Voltage: 4.5V ~ 12V DC 5. Dropout Voltage: ~1V ~ 1.3V

blocks.text: The HW-122 is a small power module built around the AMS1117-3.3 low-dropout (LDO) linear regulator. It converts a 4.5V to 12V DC input into a stable 3.3V output, ideal for powering ESP8266 and ESP32 modules, NRF24L01 radios, sensors and other 3.3V devices from a 5V USB supply or a battery pack. On-board filter capacitors and a red power LED make it ready to use.
Pins: VIN, GND, VOUT, GND (2.54mm pitch)
On board: SMD filter capacitors and red power LED
VIN: to the input supply, for example 5V from USB or an Arduino 5V pin
GND: to the ground of the supply and of the 3.3V device (common ground)
VOUT: to the 3.3V / VCC pin of your module or sensor

A linear regulator turns the extra voltage into heat: P = (Vin − 3.3V) × I. From 5V at 300mA: (5 − 3.3) × 0.3 ≈ 0.5W, which this small board handles. From 12V at 300mA: (12 − 3.3) × 0.3 ≈ 2.6W, which is too much heat. For high currents, feed the module from 5V or use a buck converter from 12V.
3.3V sensors, displays and SD card modules

ekostra-3125.summary: 220uF 50V Radial Electrolytic Capacitor 1. Capacitance: 220µF 2. Voltage Rating: 50V DC 3. Capacitance Tolerance: ±20% (typical) 4. Mounting Type: Through-Hole Radial 5. Operating Temperature: -40°C to +85°C 6. Polarity: Polarized (marked case)

blocks.text: This 220µF 50V radial electrolytic capacitor is designed for high-voltage decoupling and filtering in circuits operating on 24V, 36V, or 48V DC buses. The 50V rating provides robust voltage endurance for industrial and automotive applications, where transient voltages may exceed nominal rail levels, while the 220µF value offers sufficient bulk capacitance for many medium-power stages.

Constructed as a polarized aluminum electrolytic capacitor with radial leads, it is intended for vertical through-hole PCB mounting. The higher voltage rating results in a larger case size than lower-voltage types, but delivers the dielectric strength and ripple handling needed for demanding power environments.
Radial leads for standard PCB insertion

The PICkit3 USB PIC Microcontroller Programmer/Debugger with ZIF Socket Adapter is a low-cost in-circuit programming tool for PIC and dsPIC Flash microcontrollers, built around the same core as Microchip’s official PICkit 3. It connects to a PC via USB and to the target chip through ICSP, and the bundled ZIF socket adapter lets you program bare chips off-board.
USB Interface: Connects to a PC via a standard USB Type-A to Mini-USB cable for programming and power.
In-Circuit Programming: Supports both in-circuit programming through a 6-pin ICSP header and off-board programming via the ZIF socket.
Broad Device Support: Compatible with a wide range of PIC, dsPIC, PIC24 and PIC32 microcontrollers.
Status Indicators: Onboard Power, Active and Status LEDs show connection and programming state at a glance.
IDE Integration: Works with MPLAB X IDE for programming, debugging and Programmer-To-Go operation.

The Arduino Nano Terminal Adapter Shield is a simple breakout board that plugs onto an Arduino Nano and brings every digital and analog pin out to labeled screw terminals. It removes the need for a breadboard when wiring sensors, motors, and other peripherals to a Nano-based project.
Full Pin Breakout: Exposes all digital I/O, analog inputs, power, and ground pins from the Arduino Nano.
Screw Terminal Blocks: Secure, tool-tightened connections replace loose jumper wires for a more reliable build.
Direct Socket Mounting: Two rows of female headers let the Nano plug straight into the shield with no soldering.
Clear Pin Labeling: Every terminal is silkscreened with its matching Nano pin name for fast, mistake-free wiring.
Compact Layout: Matches the small footprint of the Nano, keeping the assembled board easy to mount in enclosures.
